text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Communist Party Secretary General Do Muoi said Vietnam's party and government regarded the consolidation of multi-faceted cooperation with China as an important part of its foreign policy. Muoi reiterated that Vietnam recognized the People's Republic of China Government as the only legitimate representative for all China, including Taiwan.
-- The government wants the Ministry of Finance to cut at least 30 percent off individual budgets initially earmarked as funds for entertainment in an attempt to balance this year's state budget.
-- The Ministry of Trade will ask the European Union to grant Vietnam 6-10 percent of its garment export quota for 1998 in advance to help local textile companies.
-- The World Bank pledged $145 million in soft loans for the period from 1997 to 2000 to help upgrade and develop the distribution power grid in Ho Chi Minh City.
-- The Communist Party's Politburo has instructed all party cells to implement resolutions on building a strong socialist state, expanding democracy and developing a personnel strategy.
-- Vietnam earned $369 million from exports of aquatic products in the first half of this year.
-- Chinese Party leader and President Jiang Zemin has accepted an invitation to visit Vietnam.
-- Hanoi will set up a special fund to develop it's infrastructure.
-- Iran and Belarus will buy 21,000 tonnes of rubber from Vietnam.
